propositions: Writes to the link store are keyed on (target_id, relation), allowing one pair to hold multiple differently-related dependencies simultaneously, but removal is pair-scoped with no relation parameter, causing asymmetry

Guard G5 in _inbound_unlink_one declines to remove inbound records when the pair's net-active relation does not match the vanished peer relation, leading to permanent non-convergence and repeated re-emission of the removal record

The outbound differ deduplicates on (vendor_type, target_key) direction-agnostically without deduping on relation, preventing outbound re-adds from suppressing inbound removal records when remote and local links differ in direction but share the same vendor type

Inbound link removal for double-related pairs never reaches a terminal state: the removal record re-emits and re-declines on every reconcile pass, visible only as a log line with no operator-visible convergence failure

The fix makes removal symmetric with writes by adding a relation-scoped removal seam at the graph layer, keyed on (target_id, relation), and updating _inbound_unlink_one to use it so G5-reached cases converge instead of declining
CLI unlink gains an optional relation argument; with no relation the existing pair-scoped most-recent behavior is unchanged for backward compatibility
